7.1.basis: The evidence shows China has a dedicated, comprehensive statute—the Personal Information Protection Law—with foundational articles (Arts. 1, 2, 4) establishing its purpose, scope, and definitions covering personal information processing broadly. This indicates a horizontal, comprehensive legal framework rather than an absence or merely sectoral regulation.
7.1.controlling_law: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法 (Personal Information Protection Law of the PRC)

7.2.basis: The evidence shows China's Cybersecurity Law is a broadly applicable (horizontal), comprehensive statute covering scope, principles, network operator obligations, security protections, and incident/emergency provisions (Arts. 1,2,4,5,6,9,11,23,53,55,57), supplemented by sectoral regulations for critical information infrastructure (关键信息基础设施安全保护条例) and legacy computer system protection rules. This constitutes a dedicated, comprehensive cybersecurity legal framework rather than an absence or mere sectoral patchwork, so the inverted indicator scores 0 (framework exists).
7.2.controlling_law: 中华人民共和国网络安全法 (Cybersecurity Law of the PRC)
